words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens 18:23 as continuation, not a fresh detached maxim. It carries the restraint of 18:22 into another prohibition, so the movement runs from disputing and soliciting claims about the Sleepers to refusing unqualified future self-assertion. The opening conjunction also begins the outer frame that will close on {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}), placing the quoted claim between restraint and future uncertainty.

topics.headline: continued prohibition chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is a third member of an instruction chain, not isolated advice about phrasing.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as coordination, and the CRITICAL rows tie it to the immediately prior prohibitions in 18:22.

topics.headline: opening restraint frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's shape: prohibition opens the utterance and future time closes it.
topics.reason: The summary row is locally supported because {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) plus the following prohibition opens the frame and {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}) is the final temporal word.

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) is prohibitive rather than merely negative. It reaches through {{ar:تَقُولَنَّ}} ({{tr:taqulanna}}) to the embedded sentence {{ar:إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا}} ({{tr:inni fa’ilun dhalika ghadan}}), so the banned act is producing the whole unqualified future-agency declaration. Its separate visibility before the verb lets the listener parse restraint first, before the doubled verbal ending tightens the command.

topics.headline: prohibition over the whole quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle governs an utterance template, not just a single verb.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment evidence identify prohibitive force and the quoted complement governed by the speech verb.

topics.headline: sound of tightening restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears an acoustic movement from open prohibition into the compressed emphatic verb.
topics.reason: The sound row is consistent with the local sequence from {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) into {{ar:تَقُولَنَّ}} ({{tr:taqulanna}}); it is a phonetic payoff, not a separate grammar claim.

words.gloss_range: emphatic second-person prohibition against uttering a future-agency claim
words.root_gloss_range: saying, uttering, declaring, reporting, holding an articulated opinion; the local quote selects outward declaration

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing the emphatic speech verb
first-person opening of the quoted clause

words.prose: {{ar:تَقُولَنَّ}} ({{tr:taqulanna}}) carries the main speech prohibition with unusual pressure: prohibitive {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) governs an imperfect verb whose final doubled nūn makes the ban emphatic. The second-person form addresses the listener before the quoted content shifts into {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:inni}}), so the grammar says, in effect, do not let your mouth become the source of this first-person claim. The root range can include speech, opinion, and report, but the embedded clause narrows it here to an outward declaration about doing, an utterance that moves from speech to thing to agency to tomorrow. The supplied 17:23 parallel makes this a familiar q-w-l speech-restraint pattern, while 18:23 makes the pattern heavier by attaching the emphatic ending to a ban on future self-assertion.

topics.headline: jussive imperfect with heavy emphasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb form makes the command severe while still targeting future or repeatable utterance.
topics.reason: QAC marks the prohibitive frame and energetic nūn, matching the CRITICAL morphology rows.

topics.headline: you must not say I
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the role movement from an addressed second person into the prohibited first-person sentence.
topics.reason: The verb has controlled second-person subject agreement, while {{ar:إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا}} ({{tr:inni fa’ilun dhalika ghadan}}) is the quoted complement.

topics.headline: qawl narrowed to outward declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah targets verbalized certainty, not the mere existence of a plan or inner intention.
topics.reason: The broader root can cover speech, opinion, and inner saying, but the local quoted clause selects declared speech as the active branch.

topics.headline: speech-ban pattern across references
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is a familiar speech-restraint pattern made heavier for future self-assertion.
topics.reason: The 17:23 comparison is concrete and limited: both use q-w-l prohibition, while 18:23 intensifies the form with the heavy ending on {{ar:تَقُولَنَّ}} ({{tr:taqulanna}}).

topics.headline: speech becomes a claimed act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's escalation from saying, to any matter, to doer-status, to future time.
topics.reason: The local sequence links {{ar:تَقُولَنَّ}} ({{tr:taqulanna}}), {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}), {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}), and {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}) in one syntactic chain.

words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) is the small hinge that prevents the quote from arriving too soon. It governs {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) and attaches that phrase to {{ar:تَقُولَنَّ}} ({{tr:taqulanna}}), so the forbidden saying is first marked as speech about or on account of some matter. Topic is the locally strongest reading, while purpose or occasion remains a secondary pressure: any matter can become the occasion for the unqualified claim.

topics.headline: lām makes the thing the speech topic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah establishes the domain of speech before the speaker asserts agency.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) as the governed complement of the preposition tied to the speech verb.

topics.headline: topic with purpose or occasion pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lām broadens the ban from one quoted example to any matter that might occasion such a claim.
topics.reason: The local attachment licenses a topic relation most strongly; purpose or cause is retained only as secondary pressure, not as a replacement parse.

topics.headline: short vowel cues dependence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the prepositional dependency before the broad noun appears.
topics.reason: The kasra-bearing form of {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) immediately prepares the governed noun {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}).

words.gloss_range: indefinite governed noun with maximal matter scope, later resumed by the demonstrative
words.root_gloss_range: thing, matter, affair, conceivable object, and in adjacent root-family evidence will or willing; local sense is a broad matter or thing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the broad matter noun

words.prose: {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) is governed by {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}), so it first functions as the matter of speech rather than the object of action. Its singular tanwīn keeps the scope distributively open: any one matter can fall under the ban. The later {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) loops back to it, turning the broad topic into the exact 'that' claimed inside the quote. The root-family link to willing is useful only as a forward pressure toward 18:24, where the required qualification invokes divine willing; it does not turn this noun itself into a verb of will. Its recurrence in 18:70, 18:71, 18:74, and 18:76 keeps the broad noun inside a Cave-surah pattern about limits on speaking and asking, and its tanwīn joins the audible indefinite thread with {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}) and {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}).

topics.headline: any thing becomes that thing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the broad matter is not left vague; it is later resumed as the object-domain of the agency claim.
topics.reason: The cross-reference evidence forces {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) to point back to {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}).

topics.headline: singular indefinite universality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no class of undertaking is excluded; the singular noun works item by item across any possible matter.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as indefinite genitive, and the CRITICAL rows coherently read its tanwīn as widening scope.

topics.headline: thing answered by willing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claimed thing is already near the lexical field that the next ayah will use to qualify future speech.
topics.reason: The root-family evidence supports an echo toward 18:24, but local grammar keeps the word as the noun 'thing' or 'matter,' not as the verb of willing.

topics.headline: surah recurrence and tanwīn thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this broad noun belongs both to a Cave-surah pattern of limits on speaking and to the ayah's audible indefinite chain.
topics.reason: The recurrence references 18:70, 18:71, 18:74, and 18:76, while the local sound row links {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) with {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}) and {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}).

words.root_display: no lexical root (emphatic particle with first-person suffix)
words.gloss_range: emphatic first-person opening of the quoted clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: predicate naming the agency claimed by the first-person speaker

words.prose: {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:inni}}) opens the exact forbidden sentence. The particle and first-person suffix are fused, so confirmation and self-reference arrive together: the quote begins by centering 'I' before {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}) names the agency being claimed. This is the pivot from the outer second-person prohibition to the inner first-person voice, and the 2:30 comparison sharpens the contrast: the same emphatic first-person frame has different force when the speaker and agency claim are divine rather than human.

topics.headline: asserted first-person agency opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted claim starts by binding emphasis to the speaker's self-reference.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:inni}}) as the subject side of the nominal clause whose predicate is {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}).

topics.headline: outer you becomes inner I
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rhetorical pivot: the command addresses you, then makes you hear the banned sentence as I.
topics.reason: The boundary rows and syntax both support the shift from reported others in 18:22 to self-speech in 18:23.

topics.headline: same frame, different speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that emphatic first-person agency language cannot be evaluated apart from who is speaking.
topics.reason: The comparison is limited to the supplied 2:30 frame: {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:inni}}) plus an agent predicate is not rejected as a form, but as an unqualified human claim in 18:23.

words.gloss_range: active participle predicate claiming doer-status over the resumed matter
words.root_gloss_range: doing, acting, bringing about, producing an effect; local form is the active agent noun, not passive result or causative activation

words.prose: {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}) is the predicate that makes {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:inni}}) a claim of agency. Because it is an active participle rather than a finite future verb, the speaker is not merely saying that an act may occur; the wording presents the self as the doer over {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) and toward {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}). The form should not be stretched into causative Form II or passive accomplishment: its force is active agent-role, with the broader f-ʿ-l field of action and effect concentrated in the claim to occupy the doer position. The supplied 2:30 and 17:108 contrasts also keep human projected agency distinct from divine making and accomplished enactment, and the tanwīn on the predicate binds the claimed doer into the same indefinite sound thread as the thing and tomorrow.

topics.headline: active predicate makes agency central
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted sentence asserts agent identity, not merely a future event.
topics.reason: The word is the khabar of {{ar:إِنِّي}} ({{tr:inni}}), so it supplies the agency asserted by the quoted clause.

topics.headline: active participle, not causative or passive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exactly what kind of agency is being claimed: simple active doer-status, not overt causation or completed passive result.
topics.reason: V4 supplies other branches and forms, but the local surface is the simple active participle and blocks importing Form II activation or passive accomplishment as the local sense.

topics.headline: agency reaches the resumed matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doer-claim takes hold of the earlier thing through the delayed demonstrative object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) the object of {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}), routing the earlier matter into the action claim.

topics.headline: human claim versus enacted certainty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a contrast between human projected agency and frames of divine making or accomplished enactment.
topics.reason: The 2:30 and 17:108 comparisons are retained as contrasts in agency framing, without letting them override the local human quote in 18:23.

topics.headline: doer joins the indefinite sound chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the claimed doer bound into the same indefinite cadence as the thing and tomorrow.
topics.reason: The tanwīn on {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}) audibly links it with {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) and {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}).

words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) closes the local reference loop. The quote has already asserted {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}); this demonstrative then supplies the object-like pointer, sending the claim back to {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) rather than introducing a new object. Its definiteness and masculine singular form make the broad 'any matter' become that same matter inside the quote. Its deictic distance also fits a claim projected toward {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}), though the local grammar remains referential before it becomes symbolic.

topics.headline: demonstrative resumes the earlier matter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sentence is self-contained: about any thing, I am a doer of that thing.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly resolves {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhalika}}) back to {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) and makes it the object of the active participle.

topics.headline: that across distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pointer is not a near-this gesture but a that-pointer suited to a future-directed claim.
topics.reason: The distance payoff survives because the demonstrative points back while {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}) projects the claimed act forward; it remains secondary to the forced local reference.

topics.headline: visible pointer inside speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pointer arrives after the agent predicate and makes the forbidden speech precise.
topics.reason: The distribution and same-surah rows support salience, while the local order {{ar:فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا}} ({{tr:fa’ilun dhalika ghadan}}) explains the delayed object pointer.

words.gloss_range: accusative time adverb closing the quoted claim on tomorrow or the proximate future
words.root_gloss_range: tomorrow, the morrow, early-day departure, and future horizon; local form is an adverb of time, not a finite movement verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nominal agency statement completed by the time adverb

words.prose: {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}) is the final landing of the quoted claim. As an accusative time adverb, it supplies the future timing for the nominal agency statement {{ar:إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:inni fa’ilun dhalika}}); the claim is not just 'I am a doer' but 'I am a doer of that tomorrow.' The gh-d-w root gives tomorrow a morning-departure horizon, the first step beyond present control, while local grammar keeps it an adverb of time rather than a verb of setting out. Its final position makes the ayah end on the very future that the next ayah, 18:24, will qualify by divine willing. In the supplied 59:18 contrast, tomorrow is the horizon for what has been prepared; here it is the horizon one must not claim to control. The final -an also completes the indefinite nasal cadence that has linked matter, doer, and future time.

topics.headline: tomorrow completes the forbidden quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that future time belongs inside the banned utterance and completes its scope.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}) the adverbial modifier of {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}) inside the quoted complement.

topics.headline: tomorrow as first outward horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that tomorrow is felt as the first step beyond present control, not just a neutral date stamp.
topics.reason: The root supports morning, morrow, and departure imagery; local grammar narrows the active sense to a time adverb for tomorrow or proximate future, not a narrated act of going out.

topics.headline: claiming tomorrow versus accountable future
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the unqualified claim over tomorrow is set against other future-orientation frames and awaits the next ayah's exception.
topics.reason: The 59:18 comparison contrasts preparing for tomorrow with claiming control of tomorrow, and the 18:24 bridge explains why the final future word awaits qualification.

topics.headline: future as audible closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah close with the same indefinite nasal thread that linked matter, doer, and time.
topics.reason: The final position of {{ar:غَدًا}} ({{tr:ghadan}}) and its tanwīn connect it to the earlier indefinite sounds on {{ar:شَا۟ىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay’in}}) and {{ar:فَاعِلٌ}} ({{tr:fa’ilun}}).

baseline_models.mechanism: The utterance takes a reportable thing, installs the speaker as its producer, and closes the claim onto the next day. Speech makes absent agency sound presently secured.

activation_trace.role: Spoken utterance supplies the public assertion intercepted by the emphatic prohibition.
A knowable, reportable thing supplies the deed's apparently determinate object.
Producing an act supplies the causal role claimed by the active participle.
The following day supplies the absent time treated as already settled.

changed_reading.before: A general ban on saying that one will do something tomorrow.
changed_reading.after: A ban on using present speech to authorize oneself as the secured producer of an event across an unpossessed temporal boundary.

baseline_models.mechanism: The root-domain of the object also carries willing, while the active participle names realized agency. The categorical sentence collapses object, intention, capacity, permission, and occurrence into one self-attribution.

activation_trace.role: Will attached to a thing exposes volition as a distinct hinge inside the named object.
Actual production supplies the outcome that speech prematurely fuses with willing.
A saying as a held position gives the forecast the force of committed belief.

changed_reading.before: Do not omit a pious qualification from a future plan.
changed_reading.after: Do not compress the several contingencies between wanting a thing and bringing it about into the identity claim 'I am its doer.'

baseline_models.mechanism: The tomorrow-root carries both the next day and morning departure. The speaker's current declaration rhetorically arrives before the temporal going has occurred.

activation_trace.role: Morning departure images the future as movement that still has to be traversed.
The next day supplies the far side of that still-open passage.
The active producer supplies the identity projected across the passage.

changed_reading.before: Tomorrow is a date on which the speaker schedules an act.
changed_reading.after: Tomorrow is an untraversed passage, so present speech must not treat arrival and agency on its far side as possessions.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier speech is traced from missing knowledge through a word leaving mouths into false saying. Applied to the focus, the emphatic ban guards the boundary where an internal plan is externalized in the grammatical shape of a known fact.

activation_trace.role: Unshown inner speech supplies the plan before it crosses into public assertion.
Knowledge as disclosure supplies the warrant explicitly missing from the earlier speakers.
Bringing something out of concealment supplies the transition from inward content to exposed word.
Opening the mouth in speech locates the physical threshold of externalization.
Saying what has not been supplies the precise risk of granting an unrealized event factual status.
Contradiction of truth supplies the endpoint against which overconfident future speech is measured.

structural_cues: 18:5 orders absent knowledge, a word exiting mouths, saying, and falsehood; 18:23 places an emphatic prohibition at the same speech boundary.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the externalization sequence; I infer that a future plan can counterfeit event-status when uttered categorically. A live alternative is that such speech is not false but merely insufficiently qualified.

changed_reading.before: The speaker should append a formula to an otherwise ordinary forecast.
changed_reading.after: The speaker must control the conversion of inward intention into outward fact-claim before knowledge of occurrence exists.

context_deltas.mechanism: The field of action is made as adornment, used to reveal quality of work, and then made stripped away. A future deed is therefore performance inside a mutable test environment, not a product the agent already owns.

activation_trace.role: Producing an act supplies the focus claim whose ownership is being tested.
A trial that reveals condition makes deed-quality, rather than guaranteed occurrence, the operative measure.
Purposeful work supplies the action evaluated within the test.
Making a thing enter another state supplies environmental mutability beyond the agent.
Cutting and extirpation supplies the reversal that can remove the deed's apparent field.

structural_cues: 18:7-8 moves from adorned earth, through testing of work, to a stripped surface.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a made, tested, and reversed action-field; I infer that this destabilizes self-ownership of tomorrow's deed. The alternative is that the sequence concerns moral quality only, not ordinary planning.

changed_reading.before: The problem is certainty about whether a scheduled act will occur.
changed_reading.after: The deeper mistake is treating a tested deed and its mutable field as an already owned output instead of attending to the quality revealed if action becomes possible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The cave sequence suspends agents, raises them, leaves them unable to measure their duration, and then sends them into concrete action. It separates present capacity to act from authority to guarantee an uninterrupted self across time.

activation_trace.role: The active producer supplies the continuous future identity put under pressure.
The following day supplies the temporal gap across which continuity is claimed.
Arousing the still from repose supplies an externally restored capacity for agency.
Remaining in place supplies elapsed duration unavailable to the sleepers' control.
A duration's terminal limit supplies the interval they cannot independently know.
A span of time supplies their radically compressed estimate of experienced duration.
Disclosed knowledge assigned to their Lord supplies the correction to self-measurement.
Sending a delegate supplies practical action that resumes without a claim to temporal mastery.

structural_cues: 18:11-19 inserts suspension, reawakening, disputed duration, and a practical errand between intention and action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies interrupted agency and failed self-timing; I apply that discontinuity to the identity claim 'I am doing that tomorrow.' A live alternative confines the discontinuity to the story's miracle.

changed_reading.after: The verse denies that the present speaker can guarantee the continuity of self, capacity, and clock required to become tomorrow's agent, while still permitting concrete action when capacity is present.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context does not reject all future reference: it affirms God's promise as true and assigns knowledge of tarrying and the unseen to God. The focus prohibition therefore ranks future claims by warrant and authority rather than banning futurity as grammar.

activation_trace.role: Utterance supplies the human future claim whose warrant is assessed.
The next day supplies the future horizon under dispute.
A promise opening hope by speech supplies a warranted form of future assertion.
Truth fixed in correspondence with reality supplies the promise's validated status.
Knowledge as disclosure assigns accurate duration-knowledge beyond the human counters.
What is hidden from sight supplies the domain to which tomorrow belongs.

structural_cues: 18:21 validates a divine promise; 18:26 closes the unit by assigning duration-knowledge and the unseen to God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies valid future promise and asymmetrical knowledge; I infer a hierarchy of warrant between divine promise and human self-prediction. The alternative is a looser thematic contrast without a rule for human speech.

changed_reading.after: Future claims are not equal: certainty requires warrant proportionate to hidden time, and the speaker lacks warrant to guarantee personal execution.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated speculative 'they will say' immediately precedes 'do not surely say,' and the count is named as casting speech at the unseen. The focus transfers that epistemic discipline from hidden history to the speaker's hidden future self.

activation_trace.role: Saying that operates like supposition exposes the predictive force inside the focus declaration.
The following day supplies the speaker's own unseen object of prediction.
Repeated sayings as suppositions supply the immediate verbal pattern corrected by the singular prohibition.
Knowledge as disclosure supplies the warrant explicitly contrasted with speculative counting.
Speaking by conjecture about the unseen supplies the epistemic mechanism, not merely an image of counting.
Hiddenness from sight supplies the shared condition of the cave count and tomorrow.
Doubt and hesitation supply the dispute-state surrounding unsupported claims.

structural_cues: The sequence سَيَقُولُونَ / وَيَقُولُونَ in 18:22 is followed directly by وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ in 18:23.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a lexical echo and labels prior claims conjecture about the unseen; I infer that categorical self-prediction is conjecture directed at one's own tomorrow. The alternative limits the warning to disputed historical details.

changed_reading.before: The verse is chiefly about dependence in executing plans.
changed_reading.after: It is also epistemic discipline: asserting tomorrow's self and deed as settled can be a self-directed casting at the unseen.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same root appears first as the 'thing' attached to the speaker's projected act and then as 'wills' attached to God. The sequence reopens the apparently closed object by relocating the decisive volitional hinge.

activation_trace.role: The reportable thing supplies the object the speaker treats as fixed.
Will related to the thing keeps its coming-to-be dependent on a distinct volitional hinge.
Producing the event supplies the agency the speaker had closed around the self.
Willing explicitly reactivates the root's volitional branch and interrupts the closed action claim.
The worshipped God supplies the external locus to which decisive willing is grammatically attached.

structural_cues: Across 18:23-24, شَيْءٍ becomes يَشَاءَ before the subject اللَّهُ is named.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies root repetition from noun to volitional verb; I infer that it deliberately uncouples the thing from the speaker's will and relinks occurrence to divine willing. The alternative is a conventional exception with no semantic pressure from the root echo.

changed_reading.before: The speaker owns a definite thing-to-do but should acknowledge outside permission.
changed_reading.after: The thing itself is not closed property: its transition from reportable object to actual event remains inside a willing not exhausted by the speaker.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah does not treat failed qualification as terminal. Forgetting is followed by remembrance, renewed saying, and a request for nearer right direction, turning the prohibition into a recoverable speech-and-guidance loop.

activation_trace.role: The original utterance supplies the speech act that can later be repaired.
Bringing something back after forgetting supplies the recovery operation.
Loss of remembrance supplies the human failure state anticipated by the protocol.
Renewed utterance supplies an active correction rather than silent regret.
Gentle direction to the right path supplies the replacement orientation for self-certainty.
Temporal nearness supplies a nearer horizon sought without claiming possession of it.
Finding the right face of an affair supplies practical correction of the prior speech posture.

structural_cues: 18:24 sequences exception, remembrance after forgetting, renewed saying, and a comparative request for nearer right guidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit failure and correction steps; I infer a repeatable cognitive repair loop rather than a one-time formula. A live alternative reads remembrance broadly as devotion rather than repair of this specific utterance.

changed_reading.before: Forgetting the qualification means the speech rule has simply been violated.
changed_reading.after: The rule anticipates fallible memory and prescribes recovery: remember, resay without self-certainty, and redirect the plan toward nearer right guidance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it depends on the non-dominant ف ع ل to ء ب و mapping and a collateral غ د و branch. It remains anchored in فَاعِلٌ and غَدًا and forms a coherent generative analogy. Render it only as exploratory imagery, not as lexical translation or doctrine.

activation_trace.role: The split image of fathering, causing, and nurturing makes the claimed doer a would-be origin of the future deed.
Unborn contents and their risky sale image the tomorrow-deed as gestating and unavailable for present disposal.

changed_reading.before: The speaker claims that a future deed will be performed.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the speaker claims parentage and disposal of an unborn deed before the conditions that could bring it forth exist.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it moves from prediction to jurisdiction. It remains anchored in the self-naming active producer and the nearby branches of partnership and judgment. Downstream prose must present it as rhetorical pressure on self-sovereignty, not accuse ordinary planning of theological association.

activation_trace.role: Producing an act supplies the speaker's strong claim to causal jurisdiction.
Partnership supplies the image of sharing an authority that the closing ayah denies.
Delegated judgment supplies the jurisdictional question of who may guarantee an outcome.

changed_reading.before: The sentence is an overconfident personal schedule.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it is a miniature claim to unshared governance over the speaker's future causal field.

strongest_changes: 18:5 turns the rule into control of how inward intention is externalized as purported fact.
18:11-19 breaks the assumed continuity of future agent, capacity, and subjective clock while preserving practical action.
18:22 makes categorical self-prediction structurally resemble conjectural speech cast at the unseen.
18:24 reopens the 'thing' as willing and supplies a repair loop of remembrance, renewed saying, and guidance.
summary.what_was_special: The tight say/say/prohibited-say sequence, the noun-to-volitional reuse of ش ي ء, and the cave's collapse of subjective duration jointly move the ayah from formulaic etiquette to a discipline of speech, agency, time, and recoverable cognition.
remaining_uncertainties: How much semantic weight the شَيْءٍ to يَشَاءَ root echo should bear beyond the explicit exception.
How far the cave's extraordinary interruption of agency should generalize to ordinary tomorrow-plans.
Whether the active participle primarily marks settled identity, intended action, or both.
The two outliers depend on branch-distant analogies and should remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Future speech falsely encloses a knowable thing.** The shared `ش ي ء` B001 has variants “knowable thing” and “willing”; here the noun sits beside a categorical statement about tomorrow, then 18:24 supplies divine willing. I infer that the speaker illegitimately treats a future object as already bounded by present knowledge and agency. The prohibition targets grammatical closure over an open causal field.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Moses’ qualified promise at 18:69 showed that correct future grammar still does not manufacture capacity.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Tomorrow corrected by recurring morning.** `غ د و/B002` is the next day in `غَدًا`; `غ د و/B001` is morning time and setting out. The next ayah subjects future action to divine willing and remembered guidance, while exactly five ayat later the faithful call their Lord `بِٱلْغَدَوَةِ` (18:28). I infer that an asserted possession of “tomorrow” is corrected into a repeated morning practice whose arrival is received rather than owned. The prohibition reads as temporal discipline, not merely a required verbal formula.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:24 subjected tomorrow to divine willing, and 18:28 surprisingly returned the same root as recurring morning practice.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

Verilen çerçeve bunu genel iş yapma, yapılan iş adı ve etkiye uğrama sonucuyla birlikte doğru biçimde taşır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek, iş veya başka bir şey türünden bir olayı ortaya çıkarma ve gerçekleştirmedir.
Aynı alan, yapma olayının adı ile yapılmış işin adı arasında biçimce ayrım kurar.
Yapma, hedef şey üzerinde etki bırakıp onun değişmesi veya etkilenmesiyle de anlatılır.
Tek tek yapılan iş, iyi veya kötü olarak nitelenebilen bir olay biçiminde de geçer.

Ancak aynı kaynak sözü kapsamı kimi yerde özellikle koyunlara daraltır, beklenen yavru üzerinden yapılan belirsiz satışı ekler ve anne sütüyle beslenmeyen kuzu ya da oğlağa ilişkin ayrı bir kullanım da aktarır; bu öğeler çekirdek tanıma bağımlı katmanlar olarak korunmalıdır.

O yılki çiftleşmeden doğması beklenen yavru üzerine yapılan sonucu belirsiz satışın adıdır.
Ayrı bir aktarım, anne sütüyle beslenmeyen kuzu veya oğlağı bu adla belirtir.
